Decision 0004 ("What is explicitly NOT reproduced") deferred R-Co's BO-*/PRODUCT-OWNER persona layer "to when S7 actually starts and there is a concrete scenario corpus to validate against." .claude/agents/uat-runner.md's own "Note on scope" restates the same condition. REQ-210 (S7's closing requirement, done) confirmed both preconditions are now met: S7 is done, and a real scenario corpus exists (11 tenant scenarios across 3 companies, 18 platform scenarios, test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/). This requirement and REQ-359..362 are the deferred work whose trigger condition has now fired — not a reopening of the decision's reasoning, which remains correct as stated for the period before this precondition held. REVIEWER should confirm this reading before this requirement's dependents proceed rather than treat it as implicitly pre-approved. . SCOPE. 1. Extend the UAT scenario YAML schema with a `scope` field distinguishing `platform` from an open tenant-vertical identifier, and a step-level branching construct (`when:`) sufficient to express a login-routing example (role=PLATFORM_ADMIN / role=<tenant-role> / unauthenticated) without inventing a general-purpose scripting language. 2. Update uat-runner.md's 'Note on scope' to remove the stale 'no persona layer' sentence and replace it with a pointer worded 'as of REQ-361'. 3. task.description: Hard gate per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 1b (already read). Read lib/letflow/design/req358-uat-scope-branching-env.md directly — not CODE-DESIGNER's own summary of it. Verify against REQ-358's acceptance_criteria (below) and against the six full acceptance criteria in the Step 1 handoff (handoffs/WF02-REQ358-20260916/step-01-design.json, context.artifacts_in already includes the design doc; open that handoff too for the exact bar CODE-DESIGNER was held to). Pay particular attention to: (1) no implementation code present — the doc should carry the mix task's signatures/shapes only, never a full .ex function body; (2) the backward-compatibility mechanism is a concrete default-derivation rule an agent could mechanically apply, not an assertion of compatibility; (3) the branching construct's operator set is stated exactly (this gate should reject if it is vague enough that two implementers could reasonably build different things); (4) the login-routing worked example is fully written out, not summarized; (5) the uat-runner.md/WF-05 replacement prose is literal, ready-to-paste text, not a description of intent. CODE-DESIGNER's own report says it flagged 5 open questions (YAML-parsing dependency choice, branch-validation depth, whether facts beyond role need defining now, how credential_source is actually invoked since the script lives outside this repo, and branch-level vs top-level preconditions) — confirm each is genuinely left open in the doc (not silently resolved) and judge whether any is a BLOCKER-level gap (something ELIXIR-DEV cannot proceed without a decision on) versus a legitimate deferred/OQ per this project's anti-over-engineering norms. In particular: the YAML-parsing dependency choice is likely load-bearing for Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV cannot write the mix task without knowing what parses YAML) — if the design doc does not name a concrete choice AND CODE-DESIGNER's own note says it "needs REVIEWER sign-off", check whether this project already has a YAML dependency in mix.exs (e.g. via a existing YAML-reading mix task) it could reuse without a new dependency decision at all — grep mix.exs's deps() for an existing yaml library before treating this as unresolved.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion in REQ-358 (quoted above) maps to a concrete design element — no TBD/deferral language on any of them
No implementation code (.ex/.exs bodies) present in the design doc — signatures and shapes only
The backward-compatibility default-derivation rule is stated precisely enough to be mechanically applied by ELIXIR-DEV without further judgment calls
The branching construct's exact operator set and evaluation procedure is unambiguous
Cross-module/cross-file dependencies (mix.exs wiring, which files the runner/WF-05 prose replaces) are listed explicitly

Each of CODE-DESIGNER's 5 stated open questions is judged BLOCKER or legitimately-deferred, with the YAML-dependency question specifically checked against mix.exs's actual deps() before accepting it as open

result.summary: Design doc's own premise in §0 ('Project has no YAML-parsing dependency in mix.exs today') is factually wrong. mix.exs deps() already lists {:yaml_elixir, "~> 2.11", only: :test}, actively used by an existing mix task (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex) plus several test support/fixture modules. OQ-1 is therefore NOT a genuine open question requiring new REVIEWER dependency sign-off as the design claims -- it is a reuse decision the design should have made itself (per the handoff's explicit instruction to check deps() before accepting OQ-1 as open), including addressing the `only: :test` scoping, since the new letftow.check_uat_scenario_schema task is wired into the `letflow.check` alias (§2.4) which is not test-scoped -- a real blocker the current design does not surface at all. This is a load-bearing error: §2's entire mix task design is predicated on the false 'no dependency exists' premise, so AC criteria 1 and 6 both fail (deferral language on a question that is not actually open; the specific mix.exs check the gate required was not performed, or was performed and its result was misreported). All other checks (no .ex bodies present, branching operator set eq/in/else fully specified, backward-compat default-derivation rule mechanical, cross-file dependencies listed, OQ-2..OQ-5 legitimately deferred) look sound but are moot -- FAIL immediately per Step 1b's no-partial-credit rule.
